notes: Exact breadboard holes and Nano Matter pin positions are assumed (D4 at column 7, GND at column 4 on one side, 3V3 at column 2 on the other side); the manual's diagram image was not available, only the thumbnail photo.

The Grove relay module connects to the breadboard with a Grove cable in the photo; modelled as three jumper wires (SIG, VCC, GND) from breadboard to the module's Grove socket. The unused Grove NC pin is omitted.

Relay: Nano D4 drives SIG, powered from 3V3 as the manual states. The AC live wire goes through COM/NO so the relay interrupts the live path when open; the neutral goes directly to the socket via a wire nut (as in the photo).
The exact AC wiring (which relay screw terminals, which wire colours) is inferred from the photo and text 'relay interrupts the current path when open'. Mains voltage is dangerous.

Google Nest Hub Max (Thread border router) and the Google Home app are network/software components, not part of the wired circuit, so they are not included as nodes. The Nano Matter is powered/programmed via the USB-C cable to a computer/power source.
The usb-cable catalogue entry has no ports, so the edge to the Nano Matter has no port on the cable side.
